title: Why Microwaves Heat Soup But Never the Bowl

scenes.narration: A microwave oven does not cook food from the outside in. It targets water molecules directly from the inside out.
scenes.objective: Hook the viewer with a photoreal microwave transition into a dissected internal cavity view.

scenes.narration: Inside the oven wall, a magnetron tube generates high frequency electromagnetic waves at two point four five gigahertz.
scenes.objective: Dissect the magnetron module generating microwave radiation inside the waveguide.

scenes.narration: Every water molecule in your soup is a microscopic electric dipole, with a positive hydrogen side and a negative oxygen side.
scenes.objective: Zoom into a single water molecule to show its polar dipole charge structure.

scenes.narration: As the passing electric field rapidly flips back and forth, water molecules violently twist to align, turning molecular friction into heat.
scenes.objective: Demonstrate the alternating field driving violent molecular rotation and kinetic heat generation.
scenes.note: Illustrative - molecular oscillation frequency slowed for visibility

scenes.narration: Ceramic and glass bowls lack free electric dipoles. Microwave radiation passes straight through them cold while forcing the soup inside to boil.
scenes.objective: Show waves passing transparently through the non-polar ceramic bowl while forcing the soup inside to heat up.
